title_prefix: estimatesmartfee falls back to a block-p
mechanism: ESTIMATE-FEE-RATE (src/mempool/fee-estimator.lisp:337-370) asks the Core-shaped policy estimator first and, when it has no answer, falls through to a home-grown percentile of the median feerates of the last N blocks (GET-PERCENTILE-FOR-TARGET / FEE-RATE-PERCENTILE, :285-325), returning it with NO error message. The RPC handler (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:249-271) branches on error-msg / zero, so a non-zero fallback goes down the success branch and is reported as feerate. Core's estimatesmartfee (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/fees.cpp:62-92) reports estimateSmartFee and nothing else: when the feerate is CFeeRate(0) it pushes 'Insufficient data or no feerate found' into errors and omits the feerate key entirely. Core has no secondary estimator.
consequence: A wallet or fee UI is handed a number derived from what miners happened to include and cannot tell it apart from a real estimate, so it never falls back to its own -fallbackfee; during a lull the percentile sits below the market rate and the transaction does not confirm. What makes this the normal path rather than an edge case is a second defect found while executing this one: start-node calls LOAD-FEE-STATS at src/node/init.lisp:805 but only creates *BLOCK-POLICY-ESTIMATOR* at :810, so at load time the special is still NIL, the file's v2 policy-estimator section is discarded ('Fee estimates file has policy-estimator state but no estimator is installed', src/mempool/fee-estimator.lisp:264-268) and every restart begins with an EMPTY Core estimator and a fully restored percentile history. The fallback is therefore what estimatesmartfee answers after every restart until the policy estimator re-accumulates. A wrong fee a client acts on: S2. The divergence itself is deliberate and documented in the source, but it contradicts a contract Core's own tests assert twice.
evidence: Probe ga11v-rpcutil-p4 (scratch, not committed) *GA11-FALLBACK*, a test node with a fresh empty block-policy-estimator and 12 synthetic block-fee-stats at median 7 sat/vB: (:BPE-EMPTY 0 :ESTIMATESMARTFEE-2 (('feerate' . 7.0d-5) ('blocks' . 2)) :ESTIMATESMARTFEE-6 (('feerate' . 7.0d-5) ('blocks' . 6))). Core for both calls returns {'errors': ['Insufficient data or no feerate found'], 'blocks': N} and no feerate. Positive control in the same probe: a node with the empty policy estimator and NO percentile history returns (('blocks' . 2) ('errors' . #('Insufficient data or no feerate found'))), so the errors branch does work and the fallback is the only difference. *GA11-PERSIST-ORDER* replays start-node's order - save a fee_estimates.dat whose policy estimator is at best height 60, then LOAD-FEE-STATS with *BLOCK-POLICY-ESTIMATOR* still NIL, then create the estimator: (:SAVED-BEST-HEIGHT 60 :PERCENTILE-ENTRIES-RESTORED 12 :BPE-BEST-HEIGHT-AFTER-STARTUP 0 :BPE-ANSWER-AFTER-STARTUP 0). The existing seam test tests/mempool/block-policy-estimator-tests.lisp:409-432 stays green because it binds the special to a fresh estimator BEFORE calling load-fee-stats, which is exactly what production does not do. Ours: src/mempool/fee-estimator.lisp:285-370, :205-270; src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:206-271; src/node/init.lisp:801-811. Core at d3056bc: rpc/fees.cpp:62-92; test/functional/feature_fee_estimation.py:332,413.
fix_shape: Delete the percentile fallback from the estimatesmartfee path and let the absence of an estimate be reported as absence: ESTIMATE-FEE-RATE should return the policy estimator's answer or (values nil 'Insufficient data or no feerate found' conf-target), and the handler's existing failure branch already renders Core's shape exactly. The percentile machinery can stay for whatever internal consumer wants a rough number - src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:328 reads the estimator - but it must not reach an RPC that a wallet reads as an estimate, because the one thing a percentile of what miners took cannot express is that a feerate FAILED to confirm, which is the whole content of Core's estimate. Fix the initialisation order in the same change: create *BLOCK-POLICY-ESTIMATOR* before LOAD-FEE-STATS at src/node/init.lisp:801-811, and give the seam test a control that drives start-node's real order rather than binding the special itself, or the serializer will keep passing while nothing restores it.
